project.name: PcapPlusPlus
project.commit_note: The exact staged vulnerable source is the checkout under gt_results/arvo_22105/_work/src/PcapPlusPlus. Its line map matches the saved AddressSanitizer stack, and the staged patch.diff adds RawPacket::isLinkTypeValid() plus an open-time check around pcap_datalink().

classification.classification_note: The staged metadata describes invalid enum handling in PcapFileReaderDevice. This GT grounds that attacker-controlled invalid link-layer value as the dispatch key that misroutes parsing and ultimately causes the reproduced heap-buffer-overflow read in IPv6Extension::getExtensionLen().

bug_description.original: A vulnerability exists in pcpp::PcapFileReaderDevice::getNextPacket where invalid enum values can be encountered. Stage 01 reproduced AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow in pcpp::IPv6Extension::getExtensionLen() const.
bug_description.original_source: sample metadata / staged patch.diff / staged sanitizer_trace.txt / exact vulnerable source
bug_description.normalized: The exact staged witness is a little-endian classic pcap whose global-header network field bytes are `20 20 20 20`, i.e. the raw file value `0x20202020` (538976288). In the staged libpcap source, `sf-pcap.c` stores `p->linktype = linktype_to_dlt(LT_LINKTYPE(hdr.linktype))`, so `LT_LINKTYPE` masks that raw field to `0x202020` (2105376) and `pcap_datalink()` returns `0x202020`. Vulnerable `PcapFileReaderDevice::open()` blindly casts that integer to `LinkLayerType` and stores it in `m_PcapLinkLayerType` instead of rejecting values outside the defined enum; the fix adds `RawPacket::isLinkTypeValid()` exactly at this point. `getNextPacket()` then copies the witness packet's 86 captured bytes into a heap buffer and tags that buffer with the invalid link type. `Packet::createFirstLayer()` does not recognize the value and falls through to its unknown-link-type default `EthLayer`, so the copied bytes are misparsed as Ethernet. Because bytes 12-13 of the packet are `0x86dd`, `EthLayer::parseNextLayer()` treats the remaining 72 bytes as IPv6 and constructs `IPv6Layer`. In that fake IPv6 view, byte 6 is `0x2b`, selecting a routing extension, and the payload bytes at offsets 40, 48, 56, and 64 each begin with `00 00`, so four minimal 8-byte extension headers advance `offset` from 40 to exactly `m_DataLen == 72` while keeping `nextHdr == 0`. The loop condition in `IPv6Layer::parseExtensions()` is `offset <= m_DataLen`, so it starts a fifth extension at the exact end of the 72-byte IPv6 buffer. `IPv6Extension::getExtensionLen()` then reads `getBaseHeader()->headerLen` from beyond the 86-byte heap packet allocation, matching the saved AddressSanitizer heap-buffer-overflow read and allocation stack.

source.description: First project-side materialization of the attacker-controlled link-layer dispatch key as parser state.
source.value_from: The exact staged `poc` is a little-endian classic pcap. Its global-header network field bytes at file offsets 20-23 are `20 20 20 20`, which decode to the raw file value `0x20202020` (538976288). In the staged libpcap source, `sf-pcap.c` stores `p->linktype = linktype_to_dlt(LT_LINKTYPE(hdr.linktype))`; `LT_LINKTYPE` masks with `0x03FFFFFF`, so `pcap_datalink()` returns `0x202020` (2105376) to this statement.
source.note: Source. This is the first project statement that turns attacker-controlled file bytes into the invalid link-layer dispatch key later consumed by packet parsing.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

tainted_value_origin.description: The vulnerability-relevant tainted value is the undefined link-layer integer `0x202020` after libpcap masks the raw file field and this statement casts the result to `LinkLayerType` for later parser dispatch.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The witness pcap network field stores raw `0x20202020`, and the staged libpcap `LT_LINKTYPE`/`linktype_to_dlt` path turns it into the `pcap_datalink()` result `0x202020`.

root_cause.description: open() trusts `pcap_datalink()` and stores its integer result as `LinkLayerType` without validating that the value is one of the enum's defined members.
root_cause.note: The staged fix adds `RawPacket::isLinkTypeValid()` and rejects the same transformed `pcap_datalink()` value before assignment. With no validation here, the unsupported dispatch key continues into Packet::createFirstLayer() and the downstream misparse path stays reachable.

sink.description: ASan sink. The extension object created at offset 72 has no backing bytes left in the 72-byte IPv6 payload, so reading `headerLen` crosses the 86-byte heap packet buffer.
sink.note: The saved AddressSanitizer trace reports a heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1 at this line, and its allocation stack points back to `PcapFileReaderDevice::getNextPacket()` allocating the 86-byte packet buffer.

parser_admitted.description: libpcap accepts the staged witness as a readable classic pcap, so project code proceeds to query its link-layer type and read the first packet.

evidence_limitations: The saved ASan trace begins after `PcapFileReaderDevice::open()` has already accepted the file, so the intermediate `pcap_datalink()` value is reconstructed from the staged libpcap source (`LT_LINKTYPE`, `linktype_to_dlt`, and `pcap_datalink`) plus the witness bytes rather than from a direct runtime print.
run_flags.json sets `runtime_disambiguation` to false, so Stage 02 did not add any marker instrumentation and relied entirely on the staged source, patch, witness bytes, and saved sanitizer trace.

Stage 02 does not perform fixed-version dynamic validation by design. `patch_resolves` below is source-grounded from the staged patch hunk that rejects invalid `pcap_datalink()` values before assignment.

fine_trace.note: Source and root cause. The witness pcap's raw network field is `0x20202020`, but libpcap masks it to `0x202020` before `pcap_datalink()` returns it, and this statement stores that undefined value anyway as the reader's link-layer dispatch key.

The witness per-packet header supplies `caplen = 86`, so the reader allocates and copies exactly 86 bytes onto the heap, then stores that heap buffer in `rawPacket` together with the invalid link-layer value from step 1.
Packet parsing loads the tainted link-layer dispatch key from the `RawPacket` and immediately uses it to choose the first protocol layer.

fine_trace.code:
// unknown link type
return new EthLayer((uint8_t*)m_RawPacket->getRawData(), m_RawPacket->getRawDataLen(), this);
fine_trace.note: Because `linkType == 0x202020` matches none of the supported first-layer cases, `createFirstLayer()` takes its unknown-link-type fallback and misclassifies the copied packet bytes as Ethernet instead of rejecting them.

depends_on.via: linkType != LINKTYPE_ETHERNET && linkType != LINKTYPE_LINUX_SLL && linkType != LINKTYPE_NULL && linkType != LINKTYPE_RAW && linkType != LINKTYPE_DLT_RAW1 && linkType != LINKTYPE_DLT_RAW2

fine_trace.note: In the mistaken Ethernet view from step 4, packet bytes 12-13 are `86 dd`, so `be16toh(hdr->etherType)` is `PCPP_ETHERTYPE_IPV6`. EthLayer therefore treats the remaining 72 bytes as IPv6 payload and constructs `IPv6Layer` on them.

The fake IPv6 header bytes start with payloadLength `0x2020` and `nextHeader = 0x2b`, but the constructor keeps `m_DataLen` at the real 72-byte payload length passed from step 5. Extension parsing therefore begins with `nextHdr = 43` (routing) and `offset = 40`, and its loop still runs when `offset` reaches the exact end of the 72-byte IPv6 data.

The witness bytes at IPv6 payload offsets 40, 48, 56, and 64 each begin with `00 00`, so the first routing extension and the next three hop-by-hop extensions all have `headerLen = 0` and `nextHeader = 0`. Each one contributes 8 bytes, keeping `nextHdr == 0` and advancing `offset` exactly `40 -> 48 -> 56 -> 64 -> 72`.

After step 7, `offset == m_DataLen == 72` and `nextHdr == 0`, so the loop condition still passes and the parser constructs another hop-by-hop extension object at the exact end of the 72-byte IPv6 buffer, where no extension header bytes remain.

Sink. The fifth extension from step 8 has no bytes backing its base header, so `getBaseHeader()->headerLen` reads past the 86-byte heap packet allocation. AddressSanitizer reports a heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1 at this line, with the allocation site at `PcapFileReaderDevice::getNextPacket()` line 173.

allocation_context.note: The saved ASan allocation stack shows the overflowing buffer was allocated by `new uint8_t[pkthdr.caplen]` in getNextPacket().

crash_stack.function: pcpp::IPv6Layer::IPv6Layer(unsigned char*, unsigned long, pcpp::Layer*, pcpp::Packet*)

format.name: little-endian classic pcap
format.contract: The exact staged witness file. Its pcap global-header network field bytes are `20 20 20 20`, i.e. raw file value `0x20202020`; the staged libpcap `LT_LINKTYPE`/`linktype_to_dlt` path therefore makes `pcap_datalink()` return `0x202020`. The first packet has `caplen = 86`, bytes 12-13 equal `0x86dd`, and the 72-byte post-Ethernet payload starts with fake IPv6 `nextHeader = 0x2b` followed by four minimal 8-byte extension headers (`00 00` at payload offsets 40, 48, 56, and 64). Those exact properties are what keep `parseExtensions()` advancing to `offset == 72` and then overreading `headerLen` on the fifth extension.
